paragraphs.heading: 2.1 Cost-effective FSI framework

any analysis findings or sensitivity results

paragraphs.heading: 2.2 Governing Equations

that nonlinear material behavior was modeled if not implemented

validation or performance results

paragraphs.heading: 2.3.2 Material properties
paragraphs.purpose: List the material parameters and assumptions (E_vessel, E_FC, E_lipid, E_cal), their role as input parameters, and the linear elastic assumption used to map material to strength (E_FC^α).

any sensitivity or dominance findings

any analysis findings or sensitivity results

any new performance metrics beyond the cited validation

paragraphs.heading: 3.1 Dataset Generation
paragraphs.purpose: Introduce the dataset generation stage (Stage 1): overview of the idealized coronary model, separate treatment of two plaque phenotypes, and the uniform-FC-thickness modeling choice with justification for treating FC thickness as a scalar input.
must_not_claim: that the idealized models capture all patient-specific features
analysis outcomes

paragraphs.heading: 3.1.1 Input Parameters
paragraphs.purpose: Define the input parameter groups (morphological, hemodynamic, material), list representative parameters (as in input.csv), and state the 1,000-sample parametric design used to span the three-factor space.
must_not_claim: that the sampling fully exhausts clinical variability
any sensitivity or dominance conclusions

paragraphs.heading: 3.1.2 Geometry construction and meshing
paragraphs.purpose: Describe how the idealized geometries are constructed and meshed for each plaque phenotype and how FC thickness is implemented as a global scalar parameter in mesh/model.
must_not_claim: that meshing choices do not affect any later results (no sensitivity claims here)
any validation of geometry realism beyond the stated idealization

paragraphs.heading: 3.1.3 Boundary conditions
paragraphs.purpose: Specify the boundary condition implementation used for the dataset generation (inflow/outflow prescriptions, pulsatile waveforms, pressure settings) and reference BC files used to generate the simulation data.

any analysis results

paragraphs.heading: 3.1.4 Computational details
paragraphs.purpose: Provide practical computational settings for the dataset runs (number of cardiac cycles simulated, convergence criteria, parallelization strategy) and note the total planned sample count (1,000) for the dataset.

analysis findings

paragraphs.heading: 3.1.5 Output Parameters
paragraphs.purpose: Define the simulation outputs recorded for each sample: PSS (peak systolic plaque structure stress), ΔPSS (stress amplitude), sphere-averaged spatial reduction method, and the rupture-location index extraction procedure.
must_not_claim: any performance or predictive claims about these outputs
that these outputs are exhaustive of clinically relevant metrics

paragraphs.heading: 3.2 Vulnerability Index Formulation
paragraphs.purpose: Introduce Stage 2: present the conceptual form VI = stress / strength and list the stress and strength choices to be combined into candidate VIs.
must_not_claim: that any candidate VI is already proven superior (results belong in Results section)

paragraphs.heading: 3.2.1 Strength metrics
paragraphs.purpose: Describe the three strength scenarios under the linear-elastic assumption (strength ∝ E_FC^α with α ∈ {0.0, 0.5, 1.0}) and justify this parametrization as a parsimonious representation for screening.
must_not_claim: that the chosen α set captures full material nonlinearity
any claims on which α is empirically correct (results later)

paragraphs.heading: 3.2.2 Vulnerability Index (VI) definition
paragraphs.purpose: Define the six candidate VIs formed by combining stress metrics (PSS, ΔPSS) with the three strength exponents, explicitly stating VI = Stress / E_FC^α and enumerating the six combinations.
must_not_claim: that any of the candidates is validated as clinically best (that is in Results)

paragraphs.heading: 3.2.3 Rupture-location index
paragraphs.purpose: Specify how rupture-location index is computed (node-wise evaluation over fibrous-cap nodes; argmax of chosen stress field) and how it will be used in subsequent screening.
must_not_claim: that node-wise strength variation was modeled (strength is node-wise constant by assumption)
any outcomes from using the index

paragraphs.heading: 3.2.4 Seven-criterion screening and metric selection
paragraphs.purpose: Describe the seven-criterion clinical sign-based screening procedure applied to the six candidate VIs (sign-agreement test between input risk features and VI correlations) and state that this screening is used to select the final VI candidates (methodological decision).
must_not_claim: analytic results about which candidates pass (detailed pass/fail evidence belongs in Results)
clinical superiority beyond the described screening rubric

paragraphs.heading: 3.2.5 Surrogate modeling and Sobol sensitivity analysis
paragraphs.purpose: Describe Stage 3: training Gaussian Process Regression surrogates for the finalized VIs (report training pair counts used for LAP and CP), and state that Sobol first-order and total-effect indices will be computed on the trained surrogates to obtain global sensitivity measures.
must_not_claim: the sensitivity analysis results themselves (these belong in Results)
that the surrogate perfectly reproduces simulation outputs without error

paragraphs.purpose: Report the outcome of the 6-candidate VI screening against the seven clinical high-risk criteria and state which candidate(s) passed all criteria.
must_not_claim: that the screening constitutes prospective clinical validation
that candidates failing the sign-test are definitively invalid in all clinical contexts
any numerical performance metrics (e.g., sensitivity/specificity) not present in the referenced files

paragraphs.purpose: Present the global sensitivity (Sobol) analysis results for the finalized VIs, identifying the dominant factor group and listing the top-ranked parameters by first-order and total-effect indices.
must_not_claim: causal relationships between parameters and rupture beyond what variance-based sensitivity quantifies
that Sobol indices alone establish clinical utility or predictive accuracy
that ranking is identical across all patient-specific geometries not represented in the design space

paragraphs.purpose: Describe the spatial distribution of predicted rupture locations from simulations (circumferential vs axial patterns) and compare the circumferential agreement with clinical observations while noting the axial mismatch.
must_not_claim: that the observed axial mismatch definitively invalidates the simulation framework
that circumferential agreement implies full clinical equivalence without further validation

paragraphs.purpose: Compare the performance/importance of ΔPSS-based metrics versus PSS-based metrics in predicting vulnerability, showing that ΔPSS-based VI(s) have stronger association/importance.
must_not_claim: that ΔPSS is a proven clinical predictor in prospective patient cohorts (unless such data are cited elsewhere)
that monotonic stress (PSS) is irrelevant in all contexts

paragraphs.purpose: Report how inclusion of strength normalization (E_FC^α) and variation of α affects sensitivity results, and show that α>0 increases the apparent importance of material properties.
must_not_claim: that a single α value is universally optimal for all plaque types or clinical settings
that the observed dependence fully characterizes material failure mechanisms beyond the linear-elastic assumption used

paragraphs.purpose: Synthesize the sensitivity findings to state the implication that material properties dominate over hemodynamic and morphological factors (material>hemo>morpho) and note the top four controlling inputs.
must_not_claim: that imaging-based morphological metrics are always less useful clinically in every context
that the sensitivity ordering replaces clinical judgment or prospective validation

paragraphs.purpose: Explain the observed axial mismatch between simulated and clinical rupture locations and attribute it to the modelling assumption of spatially uniform fibrous-cap thickness (and other modelling idealizations) supported by input/assumption files.
must_not_claim: that this single modelling limitation accounts for all discrepancies in every case
that correcting only FC-thickness heterogeneity will necessarily fully reconcile simulation-clinic differences without further testing

paragraphs.purpose: List the principal study limitations that affect result interpretation (uniform FC thickness, idealized geometry, linear elasticity) and tie them to how they constrain applicability of the present results.
must_not_claim: that these limitations render the findings unusable or without any translational value
that other unlisted limitations do not exist

paragraphs.heading: Motivation
paragraphs.purpose: State the clinical and public-health importance of coronary atherosclerotic plaque rupture as the leading cause of acute coronary syndromes and its contribution to global cardiovascular mortality burden.
must_not_claim: Any novel empirical result from this study (no results should be asserted here).
Specific numerical epidemiologic estimates unless cited (do not invent prevalence/mortality numbers).

paragraphs.heading: Factors governing rupture
paragraphs.purpose: Describe the three broad factor categories that jointly determine plaque rupture risk: morphological, hemodynamic, and material (strength) factors.
must_not_claim: That any single category is the dominant factor (do not assert dominance here).
Empirical results from this study.

paragraphs.heading: Limitations of prior computational studies
paragraphs.purpose: Summarize limitations of existing computational work: many prior risk indices are stress-only, many studies use steady or simplified analyses, or small sample sizes and thus have not simultaneously explored morphology, hemodynamics and material under pulsatile FSI.
must_not_claim: That every prior study has all these limitations (avoid overgeneralization).
Any results or validations from the present study.

paragraphs.heading: Clinical implication of factor dominance
paragraphs.purpose: Explain why knowing which factor-group controls rupture risk matters for clinical measurement and prioritization (e.g., if material dominates, stiffness characterization should be prioritized over morphology imaging).
must_not_claim: Specific clinical policy recommendations or quantified cost–benefit statements.
Empirical evidence from this study presented as fact (this paragraph gives the implication rationale only).

paragraphs.heading: Study aim and approach
paragraphs.purpose: State the study aim: to leverage a previously validated cost‑effective pulsatile FSI tool to perform a large-scale (≈1,000-sample) parametric analysis that jointly spans morphology, hemodynamics and material (strength) and thereby enable VI definitions that include strength.
must_not_claim: That the cost‑effective FSI method is newly validated here (it is prior work; only cite/use it).
Any downstream analytical results (do not state sensitivity or VI selections here).

paragraphs.heading: Key findings (preview)
paragraphs.purpose: Briefly preview the principal findings of the study: screening retained two ΔPSS‑based VI candidates, ΔPSS (stress amplitude, fatigue perspective) is more clinically appropriate than peak systolic PSS, and global Sobol sensitivity shows material properties dominate (top drivers: E_vessel, E_FC, SBP, PP).
must_not_claim: Detailed quantitative results (no specific numerical Sobol indices or p-values here).
Causal claims beyond associations identified by sensitivity analysis.
That methodological validation or proof-of-concept for the FSI method is performed in this study (it is reused).

paragraphs.purpose: Summarize the study aim, the computational approach used (tool citation only), the scale of the parametric study, and the two principal findings (ΔPSS-based VI clinical appropriateness; material-property dominance).
must_not_claim: That the cost-effective FSI method is newly proposed or validated here (the method is cited/used only).
That findings constitute definitive clinical practice guidance or proven causal relationships beyond sensitivity/statistical evidence.
That the 1,000-sample analysis eliminates all uncertainty or is fully generalizable to all patient anatomies without qualification.

paragraphs.purpose: State the translational implications: because material properties dominate, prioritize measuring vessel/FC stiffness for clinical risk stratification and explain how ΔPSS emphasizes the need for pulsatile (fatigue) assessment.
must_not_claim: That a specific imaging modality (e.g., OCT) is proven to improve outcomes here (only that stiffness characterization may offer higher information value).
That material dominance implies morphology or hemodynamics can be ignored in all clinical contexts.

paragraphs.purpose: Acknowledge modeling limitations and explain the observed simulation–clinical discrepancy in axial rupture location in terms of model assumptions (uniform FC thickness, idealized geometry, linear elasticity).
must_not_claim: That these limitations completely invalidate the main sensitivity results.
That the specific magnitude of the axial-location discrepancy in clinical populations is fully characterized by these simulations.

paragraphs.purpose: Provide concise recommendations for next steps (research/validation): incorporate spatially varying FC thickness, patient-specific geometries, nonlinear material models, and clinical stiffness measurement studies; close with a final take-home statement reaffirming the study's contribution.
must_not_claim: That the recommended next steps will certainly resolve all sources of uncertainty or guarantee clinical impact without further validation.
That the present work provides definitive patient-level predictive tools ready for clinical deployment.
